concepts.note: In 1896 Becquerel found that uranium salts emit penetrating rays without external excitation.
concepts.title: Becquerel's uranium rays

concepts.note: Marie and Pierre Curie discovered polonium and radium in 1898, showing radioactivity is an atomic property.
concepts.title: Curie radium discovery

concepts.note: Rutherford classified alpha and beta rays by 1899, and Villard identified gamma rays in 1900.
concepts.title: Alpha, beta, gamma rays

concepts.note: The decay rate proportional to N gives N = N₀e^(−λt) and a fixed half-life for each nuclide.
concepts.title: Exponential decay law

subtopics.note: Becquerel discovered penetrating radiation from uranium salts in 1896, and the Curies discovered polonium and radium in 1898. The decay law N = N₀e^(−λt) describes the random decay of unstable nuclei, with half-life t₁/₂ = ln 2/λ.
subtopics.title: Radioactivity

concepts.note: Geiger and Marsden observed large-angle alpha deflections from thin metal foils in 1909.
concepts.title: Gold-foil scattering

concepts.note: The Coulomb scattering cross-section explains the observed angular distribution and the failure of Thomson's model.
concepts.title: Rutherford scattering formula

concepts.note: The nuclear radius is about 10⁻¹⁵ m, some 10⁴–10⁵ times smaller than an atomic radius.
concepts.title: Tiny nuclear size

concepts.note: Electrons orbit a compact nucleus, though classical stability problems motivated quantum atomic theory.
concepts.title: Planetary atom model

subtopics.note: Rutherford interpreted Geiger-Marsden alpha scattering as deflection by a tiny, massive, positively charged nucleus, with most alpha particles passing through and a few scattering at large angles. The Coulomb scattering probability scales approximately as 1/sin⁴(θ/2).
subtopics.title: Rutherford nucleus

concepts.note: In 1930 Pauli proposed a hidden neutral particle to explain the continuous beta-decay energy spectrum.
concepts.title: Pauli neutrino hypothesis

concepts.note: In 1932 Chadwick identified the neutral nuclear constituent with mass close to the proton.
concepts.title: Chadwick neutron

concepts.note: In 1934 Fermi treated beta decay as a weak four-fermion interaction.
concepts.title: Fermi beta-decay theory

concepts.note: In 1956 Reines and Cowan observed reactor antineutrinos via inverse beta decay.
concepts.title: Cowan-Reines detection

subtopics.note: Pauli postulated a neutral, nearly massless particle to preserve energy and momentum in beta decay, while Chadwick's neutron and Fermi's theory established the nuclear ingredients. Neutrinos were directly detected in 1956 through inverse beta decay, consistent with n → p + e⁻ + ν̄_e.
subtopics.title: Neutron and neutrino

concepts.note: In 1938 they found barium among neutron-irradiated uranium products.
concepts.title: Hahn-Strassmann fission

concepts.note: In 1939 they interpreted fission as liquid-drop splitting with large energy release.
concepts.title: Meitner-Frisch explanation

concepts.note: Bethe's pp chain and CNO cycle in 1938-39 explained hydrogen fusion in stars.
concepts.title: Stellar fusion cycles

concepts.note: Fission neutrons can sustain a self-amplifying nuclear chain reaction.
concepts.title: Chain reaction

subtopics.note: Neutron bombardment of uranium produced barium and lighter elements, which Hahn and Strassmann reported as fission and Meitner and Frisch explained via the liquid-drop model and mass-energy conversion. Bethe's contemporaneous work identified fusion reactions as stellar energy sources, with E = Δm c² governing the energy release.
subtopics.title: Fission and fusion

concepts.note: Gell-Mann and Ne'eman classified hadrons into SU(3) multiplets in 1961.
concepts.title: Eightfold Way

concepts.note: Quarks carry charges +2/3 or −1/3 and initially came in three flavors.
concepts.title: Fractional quark charges

concepts.note: Baryons are three-quark states and mesons are quark-antiquark pairs.
concepts.title: Hadron composition

concepts.note: Late-1960s SLAC scattering revealed pointlike charged constituents inside protons.
concepts.title: Deep inelastic evidence

subtopics.note: Gell-Mann and Zweig independently proposed that mesons and baryons are composites of fractionally charged up, down and strange quarks, explaining SU(3) multiplet patterns. The proton is uud, giving charge +2/3 + 2/3 − 1/3 = +1.
subtopics.title: Quark model

concepts.note: In 1961 Glashow proposed the electroweak gauge group SU(2) × U(1).
concepts.title: Glashow SU(2)×U(1)

concepts.note: In 1967 Weinberg and Salam incorporated spontaneous symmetry breaking into the electroweak theory.
concepts.title: Weinberg-Salam model

concepts.note: Gargamelle observed weak neutral-current events in 1973, confirming the theory.
concepts.title: Neutral currents

concepts.note: CERN discovered the W and Z bosons in 1983 at masses predicted by the theory.
concepts.title: W and Z bosons

subtopics.note: Glashow, Salam and Weinberg unified electromagnetism and the weak force in a spontaneously broken SU(2)L × U(1)Y gauge theory, predicting W and Z bosons and neutral currents. The mixing angle relates the couplings through e = g sin θ_W.
subtopics.title: Electroweak unification

concepts.note: Quarks carry one of three color charges, while gluons carry color-anticolor combinations.
concepts.title: Color charge

concepts.note: Non-Abelian gluon fields carry color and interact with one another.
concepts.title: Gluon self-interaction

concepts.note: Gross, Wilczek and Politzer showed in 1973 that α_s decreases at high momentum transfer.
concepts.title: Asymptotic freedom

concepts.note: No isolated colored particles are observed; hadrons are color singlets.
concepts.title: Confinement

subtopics.note: QCD is a non-Abelian SU(3) gauge theory in which quarks carry color and interact via eight gluons. The strong coupling α_s(Q²) falls as Q² rises, giving asymptotic freedom while confinement keeps isolated quarks unseen.
subtopics.title: Quantum chromodynamics

concepts.note: In 1964 several groups showed that spontaneous breaking of a gauge symmetry can generate particle masses.
concepts.title: Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism

concepts.note: In 2012 the two LHC experiments reported a new boson near 125 GeV/c².
concepts.title: ATLAS/CMS discovery

concepts.note: Observed production and decay rates are consistent with Standard Model mass generation.
concepts.title: Higgs couplings

concepts.note: The hierarchy problem, vacuum stability and possible Higgs partners remain unresolved.
concepts.title: Open questions

subtopics.note: ATLAS and CMS discovered a scalar boson near 125 GeV/c² at the LHC, matching the Higgs boson predicted by the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism that gives masses to W and Z bosons and fermions. Its scalar potential is V(φ) = μ²φ†φ + λ(φ†φ)².
subtopics.title: Higgs boson
